title: Tamil Nadu Government Services: Certificates and Land Records
summary: How to get income, community and nativity certificates, and how to check your land records.

body.text: Most day-to-day government work in Tamil Nadu happens at the Taluk office, the e-Sevai centre or online. Knowing where to go saves a lot of running around.

items: e-Sevai centres are one-stop counters (run by TNeGA) where you can apply for many certificates and services in person, for a small fee.
Many of the same services are also on the Tamil Nadu government website (tn.gov.in).
Always collect a receipt or acknowledgement number for every application.
Income certificate, community certificate and nativity or residence certificate.
Birth certificate and death certificate (from the local body or the Registrar).
First graduate certificate and legal heir certificate (through the Tahsildar).
Most certificates are issued within a fixed number of days, and you can track the application.
Patta is the record of ownership of the land; chitta shows the nature of the land. Both are kept by the Revenue Department.
You can view them online on the Tamil Nadu e-Services portal, and get a copy from the Taluk office.
An encumbrance certificate (EC), which shows loans or claims on a property, comes from the sub-registrar's office.
After buying land, get the patta transferred to your name (mutation).

body.text: 📌 If an application is delayed or refused

items: Ask for the reason in writing.
Escalate to the Tahsildar, the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) or the department.
For information about a public authority, file an RTI application; it must usually be answered in 30 days.

body.text: Use only the official website (a .gov.in or .nic.in address) and never pay a 'fee' to a personal account or UPI ID for a government service.
Keep a copy of every application, receipt and acknowledgement number. It is your proof of what you applied for and when.

practicalSteps: Decide whether the service is available at your e-Sevai centre or online.
Carry the documents listed for that service (ID proof, address proof, photographs).
Collect and keep the acknowledgement number, and track the application.
If it is delayed, escalate in writing and, if needed, file an RTI.
exceptions: Some certificates need local enquiry or verification by the Village Administrative Officer, which can take extra time.
Fees and the number of days can differ from service to service.

faqs.q: Where do I check my land records online?
faqs.a: On the Tamil Nadu government e-Services portal. For an encumbrance certificate, use the registration department's service.

faqs.q: What if an official demands a bribe?
faqs.a: Do not pay. Ask for the written procedure and the fee, and report the demand to the department or the anti-corruption helpline.

sources.label: Right to Information Act, 2005 - India Code

misconceptions.myth: I must go to Chennai for every certificate.
misconceptions.fact: No. Most certificates and land records are handled at your Taluk office, e-Sevai centre or online.
